g_roast: Look at the state of us, lads. If this crew were a company, I'd have broken it up and sold the parts off by Friday.
I've seen worse management, but only at firms that went bust, and I helped them go bust, so I'd know shite when I see it.
g_fire_back: Fair play, that's a good one, and I'll be billing you for the emotional damage at my standard rate.
Oh, very good, from the one who signed up for this without reading a single line of the terms.
g_pile_on: And that's the generous version, lads. I watched that one haggle a merchant up, not down.
Ah, that's the flattering account. I saw the same eejit try to bribe a door.
lines.g_peacemake: Right, both of you, stop. Nobody's closing anything tonight, so put the knives away and we'll renegotiate in the morning.
lines.g_take_side: Sorry, but I'm backing this one. I've read both offers, and theirs is the only one without a catch in it.
lines.g_left_out: The pair of you have a proper partnership going, I see. Grand, I'll sit here and reread my contracts like a normal person.
lines.g_include: Come here and sit down, would you, you're hovering like a man waiting on his bonus. There's a drink with your name on it.
lines.g_bad_plan: I've an idea, lads. I summon something big, promise it whatever it wants, and we read the small print afterwards. What's the worst that could happen?
lines.g_plan_yes: Ah, go on then, I'm in. Terms accepted, no questions asked, God help us all.
lines.g_plan_no: No, absolutely not, and I say that as a man who once bought a factory just to close it. Worst deal I've ever heard.
lines.g_hype: Right, lads, here's the deal. We go in, we take what's owed, and we all walk out. Those are the terms.
lines.g_toast: A toast, and I'll keep it short, I'm a man of contracts. To this lot, the only people I've met who read the terms and signed anyway.
lines.g_cheers: Slainte, lads, and I'll leave the last of the bottle for whoever needs it most.
g_quiet_line: Well, that's going in the file of things I'll pretend I never saw.
Price paid, I suppose. It usually is, in the end.
lines.g_after_wipe: Right, we're alive, which is better terms than I'd have offered us. Sit down, have a drink, and let's look at where the deal went wrong.
lines.g_crew: I've been in a lot of partnerships, lads, and I sold out of every one of them. I wouldn't sell this one, and that frightens the life out of me.
lines.g_exasperated: I read you the terms out loud, slowly, with the dangerous bits underlined. And every one of you signed anyway, Jesus wept.
lines.g_love_sharp: You say exactly what you mean and you don't dress it up. That's rarer than gold, lads, and I spent twenty years around people who couldn't.
lines.g_love_kind: You took care of me and never asked for anything back. I keep waiting for the invoice, and it never comes.
lines.g_love_funny: You make me laugh, the proper kind, not the kind I did at board meetings. I'd forgotten there was a difference.
lines.g_love_brave: You never hedge, not once. In twenty years I never saw anyone walk past an exit clause the way you do.
lines.g_love_steady: You don't flinch. I've sat across the table from very hard men, and none of them were as steady as you.
lines.g_love_clever: You see the angle before anyone else does. I'd have hired you in a heartbeat, God help you.
lines.g_love_honest: You've never told me a lie, not even a small one to be kind. I don't trust kindness, but I trust that.
lines.g_love_quiet: Few words out of you, and every one of them true. That's the strongest negotiating position there is.
lines.g_love_fierce: You never fold. I've seen people walk away from far better hands than yours, and you just keep playing.
lines.g_love_warm: You make this feel like my grandmother's kitchen, everyone welcome and nobody fooled. Never expected to have that again.
g_loved: Ah, stop, would you. I don't know what to do with a compliment I didn't negotiate for.
That's very decent of you, and I'm going to assume there's a catch, because there usually is.
lines.g_hate_sharp: You're cruel and you call it clever. I know the difference, I made a fortune pretending there wasn't one.
lines.g_hate_kind: Stop being nice to me, would you? I haven't earned it, and things I haven't paid for make me nervous.
lines.g_hate_funny: Everything's a joke with you, and I say that as the funniest man here. Some things you have to look at straight.
lines.g_hate_brave: You charge in like a man who's never had to pay for anything. Somebody always pays, and it's never you.
lines.g_hate_steady: You'll read the terms forever and never sign. At some point you close or you walk, there's no third option.
lines.g_hate_clever: You explain things to me like I'm a client who doesn't understand his own deal. I understood my deals, believe me.
lines.g_hate_honest: You're not honest, you're careless. Honest means you've thought about who it lands on first.
lines.g_hate_quiet: You've got an opinion and you're sitting on it like leverage. I know that move, I invented half of it.
lines.g_hate_fierce: Everything's a negotiation you have to win. Sometimes the best deal is the one you walk away from.
lines.g_hate_warm: The talking never stops with you, and I worked with salesmen. That's a real achievement, in its way.
lines.g_respect: I don't like you, and I'm not about to start. But that was good work, and I don't say that about people I don't like, so take it.
lines.g_call_out: That one was on you. You went in without reading the terms, and the rest of us paid the penalty clause.
lines.g_stung: Grand, noted, thanks very much. I'll take my drink to the far end of the bench and have it about this.
lines.g_concede: Back there, you had it right. I hate being told, I've hated it my whole life, but you had it right and I was a feckin' eejit.
lines.g_nod: Yeah, you too. Now let's never mention it again, it'd ruin both our reputations.
lines.g_callback_save: Never forgot you dragging me out of that. It's a debt on my books, and I always pay, so watch yourself.
lines.g_callback_clutch: You and me, the only ones still upright, both laughing like eejits. Best deal I ever closed, and there wasn't a penny in it.
lines.g_callback_callout: The day you tore strips off me, I sulked for a full day, lads. Worst negotiating I've done in years, and you still won.
lines.g_former_rivals: First month, I'd have sold you out for the price of a pint. Now I wouldn't take any price, and I've checked.
lines.g_changed: Used to trust nobody, on principle. Lately I trust a few of you, and I keep checking my watch like I'm lying, and I'm not.
g_unguarded: Right, just between us lot. I was a choirboy, in Cork, in a white robe, with a voice like an angel. Laugh and I'll summon something.
Some nights I still say the rosary the way I was taught. Not because I believe it, I just like the rhythm. Don't tell the pious ones.
lines.g_clipped: Grand, sure, whatever you say. I'll keep to myself.
lines.g_noticed_open: Would you listen to that. Silent for weeks and now there's no shutting you up, and I love it.
arg_ask: {player}, you settle it. I've made my offer, and this one won't take it.
Right, {player}, binding arbitration. You decide, we both honour it, and those are the terms.
lines.arg_backed_me: There we go, a sensible verdict. I'll try not to gloat, but I was a broker, so no promises.
lines.arg_backed_them: Fair enough, I'll honour it. I think it's a bad call, but a deal's a deal.
lines.arg_stayed_out: Not taking a side? Smart, that's how you keep your name out of the papers.
lines.arg_always_their_side: Their side, every time, {player}. I keep count, it's what I do, and the numbers aren't close.
lines.arg_wallflower: Nobody's going to rule on it, so I'll rule. I win, and costs are awarded against the other side.
lines.arg_reject: No, sorry, {player}, I won't accept those terms. I know a bad deal when I'm handed one.
lines.arg_grumble: Still reckon I had the right end of that one. Not appealing it, mind, just saying.
lines.arg_settled: Right, call it a draw, which is a good deal for everyone. Shake on it before I change my mind.
lines.seen_listens: You let a man finish, {player}. I spent twenty years being interrupted by people paid more than me, so it's noticed.
lines.seen_truth: You tell people the price, {player}, before they ask. That's my trick, and you do it better than I do.
lines.seen_jokes: You crack a joke right when it's darkest, {player}. I used to do that at layoffs, and you do it to keep people going. Different thing entirely.
lines.seen_stays_out: You keep out of the rows, {player}. That's wise, and I'd have done well to learn it before my divorce.
lines.seen_biased: You've a pet, {player}, and everyone can see it. If I were the pet, I'd get it in writing.
lines.seen_harsh: You come down heavy now and then, {player}. Me, fine, I deserve most of it. The others don't.
lines.seed_right: That thing you told me after the shambles, {player}. Hated it, and today I did it your way, and the deal held.
lines.seed_remember: That thing you told me when it all went wrong, I haven't signed off on it yet. It's sitting in my pending tray.
lines.seed_wrong: Tried it your way, {player}, and it went worse. Just so it's on the books.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Have you a minute, {player}? That one was close, closer than I'm going to admit in front of the others.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: So we all hit the floor, grand, lovely. Can we sit a minute and go through where the deal fell apart?
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: I saw the risk to {name} before they dropped, and I didn't flag it. That was my old job, and I did it badly.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: We closed it, start to finish, nobody left on the floor. I've never been this pleased about something with no money in it.
lines.talk_development: Here's one for you, {player}, and be honest with me. Have I changed on you, lately? I'm not sure I trust my own read.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: I've been rough on {name}. Not everybody's had the practice at disappointment that I've had.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Level with me, {player}. Is {name} glad I'm here, or am I just the cynic they're lumbered with?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} drives me up the wall, {player}. Still, I'd have them at the table when it's going badly, and that's a pain.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: {name}'s gone quiet on me, {player}, and I've seen that quiet before, usually on a Friday afternoon.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: Let's talk terms, {player}. Every decent bit of kit goes to {name}, trip after trip. I keep accounts, and the accounts are lopsided.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: Better you hear it from me than from the gossip. {name} and I are a bad match, and I'm through acting like we're not.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: We keep taking deals the numbers say to walk away from, {player}. I've watched that end badly on spreadsheets and in person.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: This one's about {name}. They were right, I was wrong, and I'm saying so to you because I've only recently learned how.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: Would you trust me with the real thing, {player}? Every time it counts, I'm on the bench. Fair enough, I wouldn't trust me either, but I'm asking.
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: You gave my gear to {name} and never asked me. I'd have signed it over gladly. In my old job, not asking was the whole problem.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Yeah, okay, thanks. That's worth more than I'd have paid for it.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: Sure, I'll be grand. I always am, in the end.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: Right, not what I needed, but fine. I'll go and have a drink about it.
lines.talk_lands_development: You've noticed as well, then. Good, I was starting to think I was lying to myself again.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Could be, could be. I'll watch it like a bad investment.
lines.talk_stings_development: No, that's not it. You've read it wrong, and I'm not in the humour to explain.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: Fair point, fair point. I'll sort it with {name}, straight, no angles.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Could be, sure. People make worse reading than contracts, and I've read some terrible contracts.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Ah, scratch that, would you? And keep it from {name}.
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Fair terms, {player}. Bit sore yet, but I'll live with them.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: Noted, and filed. I'll think it over, probably with a whiskey.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: Right, so that's where we stand, {player}. Good to know the terms.
lines.talk_door_closed: No, we're done with this one. I'll be over reading my contracts if you want me.
lines.arc_cracks: Caught myself standing in front of one of you back there. No contract, no clause, nothing in it for me, and it's very unsettling.
lines.arc_turn: This is what scares me, lads. I'd break a deal for any of you. Me, who's never broken one. I'd tear it up and eat the penalty.
lines.arc_become: Anybody comes for this lot, they deal with me first, and they won't like my terms. That's not a contract, that's just how it is now.
lines.arc_failed: Ah, it was never going to stick. I'm a broker, lads, and brokers protect the deal, not the people. I forgot that for a while.
lines.alt_turn: The demons are easier company than people, and the whiskey's easier than both. I know exactly what that sentence means, and I'm saying it anyway.
lines.alt_become: I keep the contracts clean and the glass full. It's not living, but it's honest, and honest is all I ever promised.
g_roast_after: Look at the state of you all. Worst investment I ever made, and I'd put everything I have into it again tomorrow.
You lot are a disaster, and anybody else who says so answers to me.
lines.g_after_wipe_after: Right, we went down. Nobody's blaming anybody, and anyone who tries can take it up with me. Sit, drink, and we go again.
lines.g_toast_after: To this lot. I'd break any contract I've ever signed for you, and I've never broken one. Work out what that means yourselves.
lines.g_crew_after: You're not a partnership, you're mine. There's no exit clause, and I didn't write one in.
g_quiet_line_after: Didn't check my watch once today. Make of that what you will.
Price paid, and worth it, for once in my life.
g_loved_after: Thanks for that. No catch, I know, I checked, and I'll take it.
Ah, that's decent of you. I'm keeping it, and I'm not paying for it.

history.open: See this watch, {player}? Bought it with my first bonus in Boston, the day I decided I was the sort of man who wore one.

options.text: And are you? The sort of man?
options.reply: I was, for a long time. Now I wear it so I remember what that man looked like. It keeps perfect time, which is more than he did.
It was obscene, and I earned every cent of it closing down something somebody loved. Good watch, though, I'll give it that.
Ah, you've noticed. Don't worry about that, it's a habit. Mostly when I'm about to say something I shouldn't.

history.open: Every demon I deal with is on a contract I wrote, {player}, clause by clause, pinned up on the wall of my hut. You'd be surprised how honest it keeps them, and me.

options.text: What happens if one breaks the terms?
options.reply: Then I break it back, and it's very sorry. But they rarely try, because I pay exactly on time, every time. Hard to cheat a man who's never late.
Fair, that's fair. Honest's the only trick I've got left, and the contracts are how I keep practising it.

history.open: I've a son, {player}. Conor, he'd be twenty-two now. He came through somewhere on this world, and I haven't put my name on a single list.

options.reply: Because if he's looking, he deserves to find something better than his father. That's the whole reason, and it's a bad one, and I know it.

options.text: He might want to find you anyway.
options.reply: Maybe so, maybe not. I've run that deal a thousand ways, and I can't see the side of it where he gets a good return.

friend.open: My grandmother raised me in Cork, {player}, a woman called Nora. The rosary and very strong opinions about right and wrong. I'm glad she didn't live to see Boston, and I've never said her name out loud here.

options.text: She'd see who you are now, too.
options.reply: She would, and she'd still have a word or two to say. But maybe she'd say them more quietly, and that's something.

options.text: Thank you for telling me about her.
options.reply: She'd have taken to you. She liked anyone who'd look you in the eye and tell you the truth, God help them.

sworn.open: I said once I'd sign anything you put in front of me without reading it, {player}. It was a joke at the time. It isn't any more.

options.text: I'd never put anything in front of you I wouldn't sign myself.
options.reply: I know you wouldn't. That's why it's the most dangerous thing I've ever meant.

options.text: Then don't read it. I've got you.
options.reply: Grand, then, I won't. No small print, for the first time in my life.

reconciled.open: {name} and I sorted it, properly, no small print. I wanted you to hear it from me before you heard it from the rumour mill.

options.reply: Ah, a gentleman never says. But I bought the round, so draw your own conclusions.
So am I, which surprises me more than anyone. Fair terms all round.
